content: Search: You Haven't Failed for Lack of Willpower If you have spent years or even decades struggling with your weight, you have undoubtedly been given the standard advice countless times: eat less, move more. Diet and exercise absolutely have an essential place in long-term health. However, because society focuses so heavily on these two factors, diet and exercise have become almost completely synonymous with weight management. When a diet fails, or when you find yourself unable to stick to an exercise routine, the immediate conclusion is usually self-blame: "I just don't have enough willpower." "I'm too lazy or weak." "I lack self-discipline." This is a fundamental misunderstanding of human behavior. You have not failed because of a moral defect, weakness, or a lack of desire. You have been trying to solve a problem strictly at the surface level using conscious effort, while powerful psychological and emotional forces have been operating underneath the hood working directly against you. The Car Analogy: You can slam your foot on the accelerator as hard as you want, but if the emergency brake is fully engaged, you are only going to burn out the engine. Conscious willpower is the gas pedal. The underlying beliefs, false hunger signals, and learned emotional associations are the emergency brake. Belief Systems, False Hunger, and Suppressed Energy 1. Limiting Belief Systems We often carry deeply rooted core beliefs about ourselves that operate like invisible filters over our daily choices. You may consciously desire to lose weight, while an underlying belief silently dictates otherwise: "I'm not attractive anyway, so why bother?" "I'm not worthy of feeling good in my body." "If I become attractive or visible, it isn't safe." "I've always been overweight; this is just who I am." When your conscious intention (losing weight) conflicts with a subconscious belief (unworthiness or self-protection), the subconscious belief almost always wins. The result is self-sabotage. 2. False Hunger Signals Over time, uncomfortable emotions can become so deeply linked with eating that they stop feeling like emotions altogether. They begin to feel like physical cravings and urges. You may not consciously register, "I am feeling anxious, lonely, or bored." Instead, your mind translates that emotional discomfort into a physical compulsion: "I need something sweet," or "I'm starving." These are false hunger signals . You are attempting to solve an emotional issue with nutritional restraint, leaving you in a constant, exhausting battle with your own body. 3. Freeing Up Suppressed Energy Fighting yourself every single day consumes an incredible amount of mental and physical energy. Suppressing emotions, arguing over what you are allowed to eat, and dealing with guilt takes a heavy toll on your system. When we address and resolve these false hunger signals and limiting beliefs at their source, that suppressed energy is liberated. Clients routinely report having significantly more everyday energy, a naturally invigorated baseline metabolism, and a newfound willingness to engage in healthy, active living without having to drag themselves through it. The Process: How We Work Together My approach to weight loss is a systematic, collaborative process designed to uncover the root causes of unwanted behavior and restore control to you. Phase 1: Initial Intake & Early Programming We begin by taking a detailed look at your specific goals, current eating patterns, and early history with food. Many of our strongest habits were formed in childhood through well-meaning adults: Cleaning your plate: Learning to rely on an external visual cue (an empty plate) rather than an internal biological signal (satiety). Food as reward or comfort: Being given treats for being "good" or when feeling hurt/sad. Eating by the clock: Consuming food because "it's noon" rather than because your body actually requires fuel. We identify these early lessons and evaluate whether they are still serving you today. Phase 2: Establishing the Foundation Before deep work begins, we establish a firm foundation built on clarity and education: Understanding Hypnosis: Demystifying the process so you feel completely secure and aware of how hypnosis works. The Secret Language of Feelings: I teach you a specific framework for understanding human emotions. Every feeling—anger, fear, sadness, guilt, boredom—has a distinct purpose and a specific, constructive response. When you learn to listen to and satisfy what your feelings are actually requesting, you no longer need food to numb or interpret them. Induction & Convincer: We guide you into the appropriate level of hypnosis and demonstrate to your conscious mind that you are indeed in a somnambulistic state, building confidence in your ability to shift state and accept beneficial suggestions. Initial Reframing: reframing existing weight-loss blockages and introducing foundational motivation. Phase 3: Addressing Beliefs, Emotions, & Patterns (The Heart of the Work) This is the core of the therapeutic process. Here, we move beneath the surface behavior to examine and resolve the root drivers: Uncovering and releasing the core limiting beliefs (e.g., unworthiness, self-sabotage, fear of visibility). Disconnecting uncomfortable emotions from false hunger signals. Resolving the original emotional reasons food became a coping mechanism in the first place. Phase 4: Resolving Guilt, Shame, and Anger Years of struggling with weight often leave behind a residue of heavy emotional baggage—anger at your body, guilt over past eating behaviors, and shame about failed attempts. In this stage, we actively clear these lingering secondary emotions so you can move forward with a clean slate, unburdened by past failures. Phase 5: Reinforcement & Custom Motivation By the time clients reach this stage, the majority find that their relationship with food has already naturally shifted. Because the underlying emotional drivers and false signals have been cleared, they no longer experience constant cravings or internal resistance. For those who still require specific structured support, this phase focuses on reinforcing new choices, building customized motivation toward a specific diet or exercise regimen, and cementing sustainable long-term habits. Satisfaction, Not Deprivation Traditional dieting relies on deprivation —telling yourself you cannot have what you desperately want. It is a constant state of denial that requires endless willpower to sustain. My hypnosis process operates on satisfaction . We do not simply attempt to suppress the behavior; we satisfy the underlying need driving the behavior. When the emotional need for comfort, security, or validation is met directly, and when false hunger signals are resolved, the urge to overeat naturally dissipates. You are not "holding yourself back" from eating; you simply no longer require the food to accomplish an emotional task. What Hypnosis Can and Cannot Do It is crucial to have clear and realistic expectations about what takes place in my office. What Hypnosis CAN Do Uncover and eliminate unhelpful belief systems and self-sabotaging patterns. Neutralize the emotional drivers behind false hunger and cravings. Restore emotional self-regulation using The Secret Language of Feelings . Significantly increase your natural motivation to care for your body. Restore control to you over your emotional states and eating behaviors. What Hypnosis CANNOT Do It cannot force or compel you to exercise against your will. It cannot physically strip away your choice or override your free agency. It cannot make diet or exercise choices for you. Once false cravings and emotional urges are eliminated, you still maintain full choice regarding how you nourish and move your body. Hypnosis does not take control away from you—it removes the psychological friction so that your conscious choices can finally succeed. content: Search: My Approach to Smoking Cessation Types of Approaches In order to achieve effective long term smoking cessation, I have developed two type of smoking cessation programs. I realize that in order to stop smoking and have long lasting even permanent results it requires more than simply addressing the behavior associated with smoking. As you may have already experienced, using will power along is not an effective long term solution. No matter what approach you used in the past, our approach does not just treat the symptoms of the problem like nicotine gum or the patch would do. Our solutions effectively deal with and naturalize the behavioral, mental and emotional aspects of smoking. Only by dealing with all three of these aspects will you achieve long term, even permanent results. As you continue to read, you will learn about our philosophy and approaches to smoking cessation which will provide you with the information you need, to decide if hypnosis is the right choice for you. I believe we have the most effective and thorough approaches to help you stop smoking in all of South Jersey. Clearing the Air In order to set realistic expectations as to what you, the client can expect when choosing our smoking cessation programs, we would like to dispel a common misunderstand people have when it comes to stopping smoking with hypnosis. I do not offer any one session smoking cessation programs. In our experience they have proven to be ineffective for creating long term lasting results. Most of the time people usually hear about one session group hypnosis sessions in a hotel, or one or two scripted sessions by hypnotist who does not have a great deal of training in advanced hypnotic techniques. These sessions claim to help you quit smoking, guaranteed. In order for these types of sessions to be effective, the hypnotist has to hit on exactly what you need to quit smoking. In most of these cases there is only about a 10% to 20% success rate. There is no time in these sessions for personal attention, and people can get distracted by others, inhibiting the hypnosis process, or not achieve any significant level of hypnosis. The guarantees that are offered usually are that you may come back and sit in another group session as many times as you would like, how ever often they come into town. Worse yet, even if a person does stop smoking with these type of sessions, the underlying cause has not been dealt with, so the problem will gradually shift into another area of your life, such as gaining weight, or other undesirable behaviors. I offer a personal one on one approach that deals with all of the aspects that cause a person to continue to smoke. I offer effective approaches to smoking cessation, but it takes a willingness to quit on your part, and a little bit of effort. Most of our clients out right quit, or experience a significant reduction in the amount of cigarettes they smoking after the first session, however everyone is different and there are no magic bullets that can guarantee that you will quit smoking after one session. Most likely you have been smoking for a long period of time, we feel it would be unethical to guarantee that you will quit after one session. If you think about that, it makes sense. For the Social Smoker My first program for smokers is a two session process which helps social smokes. Social smokes are people who have been smoking for less than ten years, typically only smoke in social situations, like at a bar, or out with friends. This program is designed for the social smoker who has tried to quit in the past and was able to do so for about a month or more, and it wasn't too hard to do. This program is designed to give these smokers the extra boost they need to finally quit the habit. I deal with the behavioral aspects of the habit and server any remaining mental ties our clients may have in regards to smoking. On our first session, we will begin by having you fill out paper work. This will allow use to get a little background information on your situation. I will also then give you a copy of our client bill of rights, privacy policy and explain our code of ethics. After you have filled out your paper work, we will then show you a brief video. This video will explain all about hypnosis and answer any questions or lingering doubts that you may have about hypnosis. You will then be greeted by your hypnotist who will then answer any questions you may still have, and gather a little bit more background information. Our first session will allow you to learn about hypnosis and begin to feel comfortable about the process. Together you and your hypnotist will gather information regarding your situation and develop a strategy to help you. Your hypnotist will guide you into a nice state of hypnosis and use methods to demonstrate to you that you are in hypnosis. Then your hypnotist will then proceed in dealing with the behavioral aspects of smoking, based on your input. When you come back for your second session, you will be greeted by your hypnotist once gain. Your hypnotist will ask you how it has been going and determine any problem areas that still exist. Based on your input your hypnotist will help you with those areas. Along with additional assistance with the problem areas your hypnotist will use advanced hypnotic techniques to server any remaining mental connections that you have concerning smoking. For the Regular Smoker Our second approach to smoking cessation is a therapeutic approach designed to eliminate the behavioral, mental, and emotional ties that our clients have to smoking. This program is designed for those smokers who have been smoking for more than ten years and those smokers who have tried to quit, and when they do they become too emotional. These emotions can be becoming irritable when you can't have a cigarette, become angry, sad or even anxious. This process takes approximately four to six sessions, however everyone is different has progresses at their own rate, so sometimes it make take longer than six sessions. This process is designed for the smoke that gets that feeling like they just have to have a cigarette. I have been very successful at helping our clients, but you must be ready to quit for your own reasons and ready to put forth some effort. It is important for the potential client to understand the emotional ties people develop towards smoking. When you get that feeling that you have to go smoke, what you are really doing is distracting from an emotion. So when you get that feeling, you smoke, and that smoking distracts you from that feeling. Over time you mind begins to associate that feeling with the feeling that you just have to smoke. I know than when man first roamed the Earth there was no cigarettes. So there is no true feeling for smoking, just the association your mind makes over time. After a while, of feeling that feeling and smoking to distract from it, you begin to experience another feeling, frustration. That frustration causes you to distract from the feeling of frustration thus causing you to smoke even more. Even after a while a person more feel overwhelmed causing them to smoke even more. This cycle is what we call the smoker's rut. Using advanced hypnotic techniques we can break this cycle and eliminate the feeling and urges to smoke cigarettes. The use of these advanced hypnotic techniques allows us not to just deal with those feelings, but un-plant the seed causing those cravings to vanish. The first session lays the foundation for success through the process. When you arrive for your first session you will begin by filling out paper work giving me information about your problem. Then you will be shown two short videos. The first video will explain all about hypnosis and answer any questions or lingering doubts that you may have about hypnosis. The second video will explain how emotions contribute to smoking and how hypnosis will help. Then, you will be greeted by your hypnotist who will then answer any questions you may still have, and gather a little bit more background information. Our first session will allow you to learn about hypnosis and begin to feel comfortable about the process. Together you and your hypnotist will gather information regarding your situation and develop a strategy to help you. Your hypnotist will guide you into a nice state of hypnosis and use methods to demonstrate to you that you are in hypnosis. Then your hypnotist will then proceed in dealing with the behavioral aspects of smoking, based on your input. It is important to realize that my approach to smoking cessation is a process. Every session builds on the last session. In the beginning we focus on building a solid foundation that is necessary for lasting success. After each session it you will find it will become easier and easier to cut down or even quit smoking. However it is our aim to give our clients realistic expectations. I find that when our clients have realistic expectations their rate of success is much greater. Although the first session will address a great many issues, you can't expect that everything will be solved after just one session. The first session prepares you for the rest of the process. Before doing this powerful process, it is important to decide whether you are going to stick to and complete this whole process. You can expect that over time that you will begin to achieve your goals, but sometimes people experience what they perceive as set backs. For example they have in mind they want to stop smoking, and early in the process, when they do slip think they're whole week is blown. I want you now to give yourself permission to be human and know that by choosing to do this process that over time, your worst day will become better than your best day is today. Give your self permission to look back and see all the things that you have done that you are proud of. All people are different; some people quit early on in the process and even forget they ever smoked. Others will have small thoughts about smoking but pass within 30 seconds, while they are still in the middle of the process. Then there are other clients who will have to put forth effort to stop smoking in the beginning. The important thing is to find out what is happening in these situations where you feel like smoking, and report them to your hypnotist. Your hypnotist can then determine what feelings are coming up and neutralize those feelings. Keep in mind that this process can be like peeling an onion; once you get rid of one layer of the problem another appears. Keep in mind that if you stick to the process there eventually will be no more layers. From the second session onward, we deal with the mental and emotional aspects that drive the urges and feelings to smoke. Using advanced hypnotic techniques we target and neutralize those feelings, returning your control to be who you want to be. If you are finally ready to get rid of cravings and be a non smoker this is for you. I also deal with eliminating and controlling stress. I will also check how the behavioral aspect is going and work on any additional aspects that need to be worked on. Another important overlooked aspect is smoking cessation is forgiving yourself. The burden of troubling your self with trying all these different methods of quitting contributes to stress that drive and fuel cravings for cigarettes. I find that once we neutralize the primary causes that prevent you from stopping smoking its helpful to remove any anger or guilt that you may feel towards you self. In doing so you will become self confident, happier and much more in control of many aspects of your life. Think about what it will feel like to release that. In our experience this goes a long way. Ready to Quit? As you can see, our approach to smoking cessation is thorough and complete. By eliminating the behavioral, mental and emotional aspects to smoking, we can help you achieve long last and even permanent smoking cessation, without creating a new distracting behavior such as gaining weight. I believe if you are willing to work with me, letting me be your hypnotic guide we can help you achieve your goal. It takes commitment and a little effort but with your willingness and our expertise you can succeed. Contact me and schedule your appointments. I believe I am the best choice in South Jersey. content: Search: Exploring the Subconscious Mind: Unveiling the Depths of Your Mental Landscape Unlocking the Mysteries of the Subconscious The human mind is a vast and intricate landscape, and within its depths lies the enigmatic realm of the subconscious. While the conscious mind navigates daily tasks and immediate awareness, the subconscious operates beneath the surface, influencing thoughts, behaviors, and emotions in ways often unbeknownst to us. Delving into the exploration of the subconscious mind unveils a trove of insights that can shape personal development and understanding. The Subconscious Unveiled The subconscious mind is the silent powerhouse that processes an incredible amount of information, storing memories, beliefs, and past experiences. Unlike the conscious mind, it operates without our direct awareness, silently shaping perceptions and responses. Exploring the subconscious involves peeling back the layers to understand the forces at play beneath the surface. Influence on Thoughts and Behavior Understanding the subconscious provides a key to unraveling the complexities of thought patterns and behaviors. Deep-seated beliefs and ingrained habits often originate in the subconscious, steering the course of actions without conscious realization. By exploring this mental terrain, individuals gain the capacity to reprogram limiting beliefs and cultivate positive habits. Dreams as Windows to the Subconscious Dreams, the nocturnal tapestry woven by the mind, offer a unique gateway to the subconscious. Exploring the symbolism and themes within dreams provides valuable insights into the inner workings of the mind. Analyzing recurring patterns or emotions in dreams can illuminate unresolved issues or unacknowledged desires residing in the subconscious. Hypnosis and Subconscious Rewiring Hypnosis serves as a powerful tool in the exploration and rewiring of the subconscious. In a hypnotic state, the mind becomes highly receptive to suggestions, allowing individuals to bypass the critical conscious mind and directly influence the subconscious. This process can aid in overcoming phobias, breaking habits, and fostering positive change. Mindfulness and Subconscious Awareness Practices like mindfulness bring conscious attention to the present moment, fostering a heightened awareness of thoughts and emotions. Through mindful observation, individuals can identify patterns originating from the subconscious. This awareness lays the foundation for intentional living and the gradual transformation of deeply rooted aspects of the mind. Journey to Self-Discovery Exploring the subconscious is a journey of self-discovery, shedding light on the intricacies that shape individual experiences. It is a process of unraveling the threads woven into the fabric of the mind, understanding their origins, and consciously choosing how to reweave them. This journey empowers individuals to align their subconscious with their conscious goals and aspirations. Conclusion In the exploration of the subconscious mind, individuals embark on a transformative quest to understand, reconfigure, and optimize their mental landscape. By unlocking the mysteries of the subconscious, one gains the ability to steer the course of personal growth, break free from limiting patterns, and cultivate a more intentional and fulfilling life. About The Author Adam Fistler is a Behavioral Change Consultant, Board Certified Hypnotist, Certified 5-PATH® Hypnotist, and former owner of the Baltimore Hypnosis Center. A member of the International 5-PATH® Hypnosis Association and certified by the National Guild of Hypnotists, Adam has studied hypnosis, behavior change, and the relationship between thoughts, beliefs, emotions, and behavior for more than two decades. His perspective is shaped by more than professional training. Adam has also lived through addiction and recovery firsthand across South Jersey and the Philadelphia region, including surviving on the streets of Camden. This gives him a deeply personal understanding of the struggle from both sides: as a practitioner who has helped others create change and as someone who has had to confront his own deeply ingrained patterns and beliefs. During his own recovery, Adam returned to the principles of hypnosis, mindfulness, self-talk, and behavioral change that he had studied throughout his career. He discovered that recovery could be about more than simply managing cravings or avoiding relapse—it could also be an opportunity to understand the beliefs, emotional patterns, and experiences that had shaped his behavior. Today, Adam combines his professional experience with the lessons of his own journey to serve clients throughout South Jersey, Philadelphia, and beyond, helping others explore the possibility of meaningful, lasting change. His approach is grounded in empathy, curiosity, practical tools, and the belief that people are more than the behaviors they are trying to overcome.             , the incorporation of gratitude practices emerges as a beacon of transformative and empowering potential.

Fostering Connection and Support: The Role of Gratitude in Cultivating Positive Relationships In the intricate dance of human connections, gratitude emerges as a powerful choreographer, orchestrating a harmonious interplay that transcends mere self-reflection. Beyond its individual benefits, the act of expressing thanks to others becomes a transformative force, weaving stronger social bonds and infusing relationships with a sense of connection and depth. This intentional sharing of gratitude with friends, family, or colleagues sets in motion a positive cycle that not only strengthens existing relationships but also nurtures a supportive and uplifting social environment. Gratitude, when extended beyond the boundaries of personal contemplation, becomes a bridge that spans the gaps between individuals. By openly acknowledging and appreciating the contributions of others, a reciprocal exchange is established, laying the foundation for more meaningful and resilient connections. This outward expression of thanks serves as a language of affirmation, affirming the value of the relationship and fostering a sense of mutual appreciation. The impact of gratitude on relationships is not confined to a one-time interaction; it sets in motion a virtuous cycle. When gratitude is shared, recipients often experience a deep sense of validation and goodwill. This positive emotional response frequently motivates them to reciprocate, creating a continuous loop of gratitude that reinforces the bonds between individuals. In this way, the practice of expressing thanks becomes a cornerstone for building and sustaining positive relationships. Beyond its well-documented effects on mental and emotional well-being, gratitude practices have been associated with tangible improvements in various aspects of physical health. The connection between expressing thanks and its impact on the body constitutes a fascinating exploration into the holistic nature of cultivating gratitude. Practical Gratitude Exercises: Nurturing a Positive Mindset Gratitude Journaling: Dedicate a few minutes each day to jot down things you are grateful for. This practice serves as a tangible record of the positive elements in your life, fostering a habit of mindful reflection and appreciation. Expressing Thanks: Make it a habit to verbally express gratitude. Whether through a heartfelt thank-you note or a simple spoken acknowledgment, sharing your appreciation can have a significant impact. This act not only communicates your gratitude to others but also reinforces positive connections, contributing to a culture of appreciation in your relationships and community. Gratitude Meditation: Incorporate mindfulness into your gratitude practice through meditation. Focus on feelings of gratitude, cultivating a sense of peace and contentment. This form of meditation provides a dedicated space for reflection, allowing you to deepen your connection with the positive aspects of your life and promoting emotional well-being. Acts of Kindness: Extend gratitude through actions. Perform small acts of kindness for others, fostering a positive and supportive community. Whether it's a thoughtful gesture, lending a helping hand, or simply offering a kind word, these acts not only benefit others but also contribute to a reciprocal cycle of positivity and gratitude within your social circles. Engaging in these practical gratitude exercises provides a structured approach to incorporating gratitude into your daily life. By integrating these activities into your routine, you not only cultivate a positive mindset but also contribute to a more appreciative and supportive environment for yourself and those around you. By consistently integrating gratitude practices into our routines, we pave the way for a more fulfilling and enriched existence. Gratitude, when embraced as a lifestyle, transcends occasional moments of appreciation to become a fundamental lens through which we view the world and navigate our daily experiences. This intentional focus on gratitude becomes a counterbalance to the pervasive narratives of scarcity and dissatisfaction. It's a commitment to finding joy in the seemingly ordinary, appreciating the beauty in small moments, and acknowledging the abundance that surrounds us. The transformative power of gratitude lies not just in its individual benefits but in its potential to reshape our collective consciousness. As we embrace gratitude as a lifestyle, we contribute to a cultural shift towards positivity, kindness, and appreciation. This ripple effect extends beyond personal well-being, influencing the communities and environments we inhabit.             Instead of focusing on what you don't want, frame it positively.
            For example, say you want someone who is fit, not someone who is not fat. What Values and Qualities Do You Want? Think about the qualities you seek in a person.

Search: Beyond Mesmerism: Navigating the Evolution of Hypnosis and Empowering Self-Transformation in the Modern Era Introduction: Unraveling the Mysteries of Hypnosis Prepare to embark on a captivating journey through the annals of time, 
            where the ancient art of hypnosis transforms into a beacon of hope in the modern world
            From the enigmatic days of Franz Mesmer, who first ventured into the depths of the human psyche, 
            to the pioneering work of James Braid, whose scientific rigor laid the
            foundation for contemporary practices, we'll traverse the evolution of hypnosis. In this odyssey, we'll unravel the secrets of mesmerism, 
            trace the path carved by visionaries like Dave Elman and Milton Erickson, 
            and explore the transformative techniques employed by modern luminaries 
            such as Dr. Marlene Hunter and Dr. David Spiegel. Together, 
            we'll debunk lingering myths, illuminating the true nature of hypnosis as a profound psychological tool. But this exploration is not merely a historical retrospective. Along the way,
            we'll witness real-life tales of triumph—case studies illuminating the lives of individuals who,
            through the power of hypnosis, broke barriers, overcame fears, 
            and reclaimed control over their destinies. 
            These narratives serve as testaments to the potency of hypnosis in our contemporary world. Yet, our journey does not end there.
            Armed with knowledge and inspired by the resilience of others,
            we'll delve into the heart of self-transformation. 
            You'll discover how hypnosis, once considered mysterious and mystical,
            is not only accessible but also applicable in your own life.
            We'll unveil the techniques, debunk common misconceptions, and empower you to harness the latent power of your mind. Join us as we demystify the age-old practice of hypnosis,
            unravel its evolution, and empower you to navigate its intricate pathways.
            Together, we'll illuminate the transformative potential that lies within,
            waiting to be awakened through the art and science of hypnosis. Early Pioneers to Contemporary Innovators Franz Mesmer (1734 - 1815) Franz Mesmer (1734 - 1815) Franz Mesmer was an Austrian physician who developed the theory of "animal magnetism,"
  which later became known as mesmerism. He believed that there was a magnetic force within the body
  that could be manipulated to induce healing. Mesmer's techniques involved passes of his hands or magnets
  over the patient's body to balance their magnetic fluids. Although his methods were controversial and later
  debunked, Mesmer's work contributed to the popularization of hypnotic techniques. James Braid (1795 - 1860) James Braid (1795 - 1860) James Braid was a Scottish surgeon who is often credited with coining the term "hypnosis."
  He conducted extensive research on mesmerism and found that the effects were due to suggestion and not
  magnetic forces as Mesmer had claimed. Braid's work emphasized the role of the mind in hypnotic phenomena,
  paving the way for the scientific study of hypnosis. John Elliotson (1791 - 1868) John Elliotson (1791 - 1868) John Elliotson was a British physician and a professor of medicine. He used mesmerism in his
  medical practice and believed in its therapeutic potential. He conducted public demonstrations of mesmerism
  and wrote extensively about its applications in medicine. Elliotson's advocacy helped to popularize mesmerism
  in the medical community during the 19th century. Jean-Martin Charcot (1825 - 1893) Jean-Martin Charcot (1825 - 1893) Jean-Martin Charcot was a French neurologist who conducted research on hypnosis and its
  relationship to hysteria. He used hypnosis as a tool to study various neurological disorders. Charcot's work
  influenced the understanding of the connection between hypnosis and psychological conditions, laying the foundation
  for the development of psychoanalysis. Hippolyte Bernheim (1840 - 1919) Hippolyte Bernheim (1840 - 1919) Hippolyte Bernheim, a French physician, furthered the scientific study of hypnosis. He rejected
  the idea of mesmerism and focused on the power of suggestion and the patient's suggestibility. Bernheim's research
  contributed significantly to the acceptance of hypnosis as a legitimate psychological phenomenon within the medical
  community. Sigmund Freud (1856 - 1939) Sigmund Freud (1856 - 1939) Sigmund Freud, an Austrian neurologist and the founder of psychoanalysis, initially explored hypnosis
  in his early career under the influence of Jean-Martin Charcot. While he moved away from formal hypnotic techniques,
  his experiences with hypnosis shaped his theories of the unconscious mind and psychoanalysis. Dave Elman (1900 - 1967) Dave Elman (1900 - 1967) Dave Elman was a renowned American hypnotist, radio host, and author, widely regarded as a pioneer
  in the field of hypnotherapy. He developed the "Elman Induction," a rapid and effective hypnosis induction method
  that allowed for deep trance states quickly. Elman's work emphasized the practical application of hypnosis in medical
  and therapeutic settings. His influential book, "Hypnotherapy," became a foundational resource for hypnotherapists,
  detailing his techniques and experiences. Milton Erikson (1901 - 1980) Milton Erikson (1901 - 1980) Milton Erickson, an American psychiatrist and psychologist, made significant contributions to the field
  of psychotherapy and hypnosis. He developed innovative therapeutic approaches, often referred to as Ericksonian hypnotherapy
  or indirect hypnosis, which focused on utilizing the patient's unconscious resources for healing. Dr. John Sarno (1923 - 2017) Dr. John Sarno (1923 - 2017) Dr. John Sarno was a physician known for his work on Tension Myositis Syndrome (TMS). Asserting that
  many conditions, especially chronic pain, were psychosomatic, he believed repressed emotions, particularly anger and stress,
  were underlying causes. His influential book, "Healing Back Pain: The Mind-Body Connection," emphasized the profound link
  between the mind and body. Dr. Ernest Rossi (1933 - 2020) Dr. Ernest Rossi (1933 - 2020) Dr. Ernest Rossi, a psychologist, has been a key figure in the development of psychobiology and psychosocial genomics.
  He has extensively written about the therapeutic applications of hypnosis, integrating hypnosis into his work on mind-body healing
  and wellness. Dr. Marlene Hunter (1942 - Present) Dr. Marlene Hunter (1942 - Present) Dr. Marlene Hunter, a psychologist renowned for her work in medical hypnosis, has conducted groundbreaking research
  on the applications of hypnosis in pain management, stress reduction, and coping with chronic illnesses. Dr. David Spiegel (1942 - Present) Dr. David Spiegel (1942 - Present) Dr. David Spiegel, a renowned psychiatrist, is recognized for his expertise in psychosocial oncology and hypnosis.
  His groundbreaking research explores the effects of mental state on cancer patients' recovery. Dr. Assen Alladin (1946 - Present) Dr. Assen Alladin (1946 - Present) Dr. Assen Alladin is a prominent clinical psychologist and psychotherapist known for his expertise in cognitive hypnotherapy.
  He has extensively researched and written about the applications of hypnosis in cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). Dr. Jeffrey Zeig (1947 - Present) Dr. Jeffrey Zeig (1947 - Present) Dr. Jeffrey Zeig is a prominent American psychotherapist, author, and teacher, renowned for his significant contributions
  to the field of psychotherapy and hypnotherapy. Dr. Michael Yapko (1948 - Present) Dr. Michael Yapko (1948 - Present) Dr. Michael Yapko, a renowned clinical psychologist, author, and lecturer, is a leading expert in the field of hypnosis
  and psychotherapy. Dr. Stephen Lankton (1940 - Present) Dr. Stephen Lankton (1940 - Present) Dr. Stephen Lankton is a highly regarded figure in the field of psychotherapy and hypnotherapy.
  As a licensed marriage and family therapist, clinical psychologist, and educator, he has made substantial contributions to the practice
  of clinical hypnosis. The National Guild of Hypnotists (NGH) (Founded 1950) National Guild of Hypnotists The National Guild of Hypnotists (NGH) is an organization dedicated
              to promoting the ethical and responsible use of hypnosis.
              Founded in 1950, the NGH serves as a professional organization for 
              hypnotherapists and provides resources, education, and support to its members.

Search: Winning the Battle Within: Overcoming the Urge The Uphill Battle The journey to overcome your challenges has always been an uphill battle. 
            Time and again, you've mustered the courage to face your issues head-on, 
            whether it's shedding those extra pounds, quitting smoking, breaking free from a harmful habit, or managing your anger.
            Each time, you're armed with determination, vowing that this time, you'll succeed. 
            Yet, there's an internal struggle, a relentless fight with yourself that seems insurmountable. You recognize that habits play a role, but it's the overpowering urges that pose the real challenge. 
            The cravings that hijack your thoughts, urging you to indulge in that favorite food, ignoring your well-intentioned lunch plans. 
            Stress, anxiety, anger, or sadness trigger a reflex, leading you to seek solace in food, cigarettes, or uncontrolled outbursts. 
            The urge whispers in your ear, tempting you with the promise that you can always start afresh tomorrow or have just one more indulgence. 
            It battles against your will, sabotaging your efforts and pushing you off course. Then, there's the aftermath of giving in – guilt washes over you, and you promise that it won't happen again. 
            But it does, repeatedly, leaving you frustrated and on the verge of giving up. 
            The root of the problem lies in relying solely on willpower. 
            The issue with willpower is that it belongs to your conscious mind,
            and you're attempting to conquer a subconscious problem with it. The Limits of Willpower: Unraveling the Subconscious Struggles Using sheer willpower to combat deeply ingrained urges is akin to wielding a small shield against a tidal wave.
            Your conscious mind, where willpower resides, is just the tip of the iceberg.
            Beneath the surface lies the vast realm of your subconscious, where habits, desires, and automatic responses are deeply rooted. When your conscious mind battles your subconscious desires, it's akin to engaging in 
            a fight blindfolded – you can't see the opponent clearly, making victory nearly impossible.
            Your subconscious mind, shaped by years of experiences, emotions,
            and learned behaviors, exerts a powerful influence on your actions, often overriding your conscious decisions. The Solution Lies in Rewiring the Subconscious To truly conquer your urges and break free from destructive patterns,
            the battleground needs to shift from the conscious to the subconscious.
            By delving into the depths of your mind, you can identify the triggers,
            cravings, and emotional responses that fuel your habits. 
            This deeper understanding empowers you to rewire these subconscious pathways,
            disrupting the automatic responses and cravings at their source. Hypnosis: Harnessing the Power of Your Subconscious Hypnotherapy offers a transformative approach by tapping into your subconscious. 
            Under the guidance of a skilled hypnotist, you can explore the roots of your urges and habits.
            Through tailored techniques, hypnosis helps you unveil the subconscious patterns, enabling you to challenge and rewrite them effectively. Unlike willpower, which battles the symptoms on the surface, 
            hypnosis delves into the core, addressing the underlying triggers.
            It's not about suppressing the urges but understanding and transforming them.
            By aligning your conscious and subconscious minds, hypnosis equips you with the tools to navigate stressful situations,
            manage cravings, and channel your emotions constructively. Embrace the Power Within: A Call to Action It's time to recognize that the battle within is not one of sheer willpower but of subconscious influence.
            If you're tired of the cycle of temporary victories followed by frustrating setbacks,
            consider a new approach. Embrace the power of your subconscious mind through hypnosis.
            By seeking professional guidance, you can embark on a journey to understand, challenge, and ultimately overcome your urges. Take the first step toward lasting change.
            Reach out to a qualified hypnotist and discover the transformative potential within you.
            Together, you can rewrite your story, breaking free from the grip of cravings and achieving the sustainable, positive change you desire. content: Search: Unlocking Wellness: The Profound Influence of the Mind-Body Connection in Healing Introduction: In the intricate tapestry of human existence, the symbiotic relationship between the mind and body plays a central role in shaping our overall well-being. This exploration of the mind-body connection delves into the profound and often underestimated influence that mental and emotional states wield over our physical health. Understanding this interconnectedness provides a gateway for those seeking holistic approaches to healing and wellness. Understanding the Mind-Body Connection: At its core, the mind-body connection refers to the intricate link between our thoughts, emotions, and bodily functions. This relationship is not a one-way street; instead, it's a dynamic interplay where our mental and emotional states can impact physical health, and conversely, our physical condition can influence our mental well-being. This recognition opens up new avenues for achieving and maintaining optimal health by addressing both the mind and body in tandem. Stress and Its Physiological Impact: Perhaps one of the most palpable demonstrations of the mind-body connection is the role of stress in shaping our health. Chronic stress, whether stemming from work, relationships, or other life challenges, can trigger a cascade of physiological responses. The release of stress hormones, such as cortisol, can, when prolonged, contribute to a host of health issues, including cardiovascular problems, digestive issues, and weakened immune function. Acknowledging the impact of stress becomes a crucial aspect of holistic well-being, emphasizing the need for adopting stress-reduction techniques. The Power of Positive Thinking: Central to harnessing the mind-body connection for healing is the acknowledgment of the power of positive thinking. Scientific research suggests that cultivating a positive mindset can have tangible effects on health outcomes. Optimism and a hopeful outlook have been linked to improved immune function, faster recovery from illness, and even increased longevity. Integrating practices such as mindfulness, gratitude exercises, and positive affirmations becomes instrumental in fostering a positive mental environment. Emotional Release and Physical Healing: The suppression of emotions can manifest as physical ailments, underscoring the importance of emotional release in the healing process. Practices like psychotherapy, meditation, and expressive arts therapy provide valuable avenues for individuals to explore and release pent-up emotions. This release can lead to a more harmonious mind-body state, supporting the body's natural healing mechanisms and paving the way for overall well-being. Mind-Body Practices for Healing: A myriad of mind-body practices has gained popularity for their healing benefits. Yoga, with its integration of movement, breath, and mindfulness, proves to be a holistic approach to promote physical and mental well-being. Tai chi and qigong similarly blend physical activity with meditative practices to enhance overall health. Additionally, practices like guided imagery and hypnotherapy tap into the power of the mind to influence physiological responses, offering alternative paths to healing for those who seek a more holistic approach. Conclusion: Recognizing and nurturing the mind-body connection is not just a philosophical concept but a pivotal step in fostering holistic well-being. By understanding the intricate dance between thoughts, emotions, and physical health, individuals can embark on a transformative journey toward healing that encompasses the entirety of their being. Embracing practices that promote a positive mindset, encourage emotional release, and foster mindful living empowers individuals to take an active role in their health journey. In doing so, they unlock the profound potential of the mind-body connection and embrace a holistic approach to wellness. content: Search: Unlocking Freedom from Chronic Pain: Harnessing the Power of Hypnosis Trapped With Chronic Pain In the tapestry of life, pain is an undeniable thread, weaving its way through our experiences. For many, persistent aches and discomforts become constant companions, diminishing the quality of life. Traditional paths often lead to stronger medications, but what if there was a different route—one that empowers the mind to heal the body? Enter hypnosis, a remarkable technique offering liberation from chronic pain’s grip, enabling individuals to rewrite their stories and reclaim their vitality. The Heart of Chronic Pain: A Deeper Understanding Chronic pain, a relentless foe, is not merely a physical affliction; it echoes the whispers of unresolved emotions. Rooted in anger, frustration, and hopelessness, these emotions intertwine with the physical, intensifying the agony. Hypnosis, as a holistic healer, acknowledges this intricate dance between mind and body. By recognizing and addressing the emotional undercurrents, hypnosis lays the foundation for enduring relief. Embracing a Pain-Free Tomorrow In the realm of chronic pain, hypnosis emerges as a beacon of hope, illuminating a path toward healing. By embracing relaxation, disrupting pain signals, harnessing hypnotic anesthesia, dispelling unhelpful suggestions, and addressing emotional burdens, hypnosis offers a complete and transformative solution. It grants individuals the key to a life unshackled by pain, empowering them to savor every moment with newfound freedom and joy. Through the mind-body connection, chronic pain is not just managed; it is overcome, paving the way for a vibrant, pain-free tomorrow.   Breaking the Chains of Chronic Pain: Embracing Emotional Wellness In the tapestry of chronic pain management, a groundbreaking thread weaves its way into the fabric of healing: the profound connection between emotions and physical well-being. As modern medicine advances, a paradigm shift emerges, acknowledging that pain, especially chronic pain, is not merely a physical ailment but a complex interplay of emotions and bodily sensations. Within this intricate dance, hypnosis stands as a guiding light, offering an innovative approach that goes beyond conventional methods, empowering individuals to reclaim their lives from the clutches of pain. Understanding Chronic Pain: A Multifaceted Journey Chronic pain, with its roots intertwined in the body and the mind, often leaves individuals on a daunting path of seeking relief. In the realm of modern medicine, a common standard of care involves prescribing antidepressants to chronic pain patients. This approach is grounded in a vast body of research and evidence, demonstrating that addressing emotions can significantly alleviate physical suffering. Acknowledging this, forward-thinking practitioners embrace holistic therapies like hypnosis, understanding that emotional well-being is pivotal in the pursuit of pain relief. The Transformative Power of Hypnosis Soothing the Storm Within: Hypnosis acts as a gentle breeze, calming the tempest of tension within the body. By inducing deep relaxation, hypnosis unravels clenched muscles, allowing blood to flow freely. In this state, pain recedes, making room for tranquility. Rewriting the Brain’s Script: Even after physical wounds mend, the brain can replay pain signals. Hypnosis interrupts this loop, empowering individuals to communicate to their brains that the danger has passed. Working hand in hand with medical professionals, hypnosis becomes a beacon of reassurance. Anesthesia of the Mind: In the hands of skilled practitioners, hypnosis transforms into a potent anesthesia. Dentists, pioneers in this realm, perform surgeries without traditional numbing agents, showcasing hypnosis’s ability to create localized anesthesia. With focused intent, pain dissipates under the influence of hypnosis. Dispelling Shadows of Doubt: Well-intentioned advice sometimes morphs into unhelpful suggestions, reinforcing negative beliefs about pain management. Hypnosis counters these shadows of doubt, ushering in a mindset of positivity and resilience. Embracing Emotional Liberation: Chronic pain and emotions share an unbreakable bond. Hypnosis gently guides individuals to face these emotions, providing a safe space for release. Breaking free from the cycle of negativity, hypnosis paves the way for holistic healing. Dr. John Sarno: Bridging the Gap Between Emotions and Pain Relief Dr. John Sarno, a luminary in the field of pain management, pioneered the integration of emotions into the realm of chronic pain relief. His extensive research and clinical expertise illuminated the undeniable connection between emotions and physical discomfort. Dr. Sarno's approach, rooted in addressing emotions as a fundamental aspect of pain management, achieved remarkable success, transforming the lives of countless individuals. Understanding the Role of Brain Signals in Chronic Pain In the intricate symphony of chronic pain, the brain plays a significant role, orchestrating the perception of pain long after its physical cause has been addressed. Our brains are remarkable organs, capable of sending signals throughout the body, including pain signals. While acute pain serves as a vital warning system, chronic pain often involves a malfunction in this signaling process. Even when the underlying physical issue has been healed, the brain can continue to send pain signals, trapping individuals in a cycle of discomfort. The Phenomenon of Phantom Limb Syndrome and Beyond Phantom limb syndrome stands as a poignant example of the brain's ability to create pain signals in the absence of a physical cause. In this phenomenon, individuals continue to experience pain or discomfort in limbs that are no longer there. This vivid illustration underscores the brain's powerful role in shaping our perception of pain. Beyond phantom limb syndrome, various conditions, such as fibromyalgia, complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS), and neuropathic pain disorders, further exemplify how the brain can generate pain signals even in the absence of ongoing tissue damage. These conditions highlight the complexity of chronic pain, extending beyond the physical realm into the realm of neural pathways and signaling. Disrupting Pain Signals through Hypnosis Hypnosis offers a unique pathway to disrupt these erroneous pain signals generated by the brain. Through the power of suggestion and deep relaxation, hypnosis can reprogram neural pathways, altering the way the brain perceives and processes pain. By guiding individuals into a state of focused attention and suggestibility, hypnosis can effectively intervene in the pain signaling process. In the realm of chronic pain management, hypnosis serves as a potent tool to break the cycle of pain signals. It empowers individuals to regain control over their neural responses, teaching the brain to distinguish between genuine threats and perceived discomfort. Through this reprogramming, hypnosis creates a newfound sense of relief, allowing individuals to experience life without the constant burden of pain. As we explore the depths of chronic pain and its intricate relationship with brain signals, hypnosis emerges as a beacon of hope. By disrupting these signals and guiding the mind toward a state of harmony, hypnosis paves the way for a future unburdened by chronic pain, offering individuals the freedom to embrace life with renewed vitality and joy. Dissociation: A Key to Pain Relief Dissociation, a psychological mechanism often utilized in emergency battlefield treatment and trauma situations, offers a unique perspective in the realm of pain relief. It involves mentally detaching oneself from the physical sensations of pain, creating a mental space where pain becomes distant and less overwhelming. Hypnotists adeptly teach individuals how to harness dissociation, using it as a powerful tool to alleviate chronic pain. By dissociating from the pain signals, individuals can significantly reduce their perception of discomfort, granting respite from persistent agony. A New Dawn: The Intersection of Emotional Wellness and Chronic Pain Relief In the modern landscape of chronic pain management, the emphasis on emotional well-being marks a paradigmatic shift. By elevating emotional wellness to the forefront of care, individuals are not merely managing their pain; they are rewriting their narratives, embracing a life free from the chains of chronic discomfort. Search: The Essence of Change: Empowering Transformation through Hypnosis Introduction: Understanding the Power of Change In the journey of personal growth, the concept of change often poses profound questions.
            What does it truly mean to make a change? As I delved into the realms of hypnosis and Neuro Linguistic Programming (NLP) to overcome my own shyness, I unearthed a profound truth: change is about choice.
            In this article, let's explore the transformative power of change, particularly in the context of hypnnosis. What Are Problems For? Have you ever wondered why problems exist? From my personal odyssey battling shyness, I learned that problems serve as catalysts for personal evolution.
            They drive us to explore uncharted territories within ourselves, fostering resilience and newfound strengths.
            Even amidst my own struggles, I discovered resilience, the ability to learn, and a deep desire to assist others on their journeys.
            Problems, in a twisted sense, become our greatest teachers, revealing facets of ourselves we never knew existed. What Is Change, Really? Clients often approach me with diverse interpretations of change.
            Many believe it involves adopting polar opposite behaviors or exchanging one problem for another.
            For instance, shyness may lead someone to desire boundless extroversion, while a smoker might seek solace in chewing gum.
            But is this radical shift truly the answer? Change, as I've come to realize, is not about swapping one issue for another; it's about reclaiming control.
            It's about having the freedom to choose without feeling confined to extremes. Navigating the Path to Change Various methods attempt to force change, relying on willpower, motivational speeches, affirmations, and NLP techniques.
            While effective momentarily, these approaches lack longevity.
            Willpower, akin to a temporary fix, crumbles under pressure.
            Motivational speeches create ephemeral excitement but fade in the face of ingrained beliefs.
            Affirmations and NLP techniques overpower rather than neutralize underlying emotions. Understanding the Solution: Hypnosis Trained in 5-PATH Hypnosis, I comprehend that problems stem from beliefs, emotions, and misperceptions.
            Unbalanced emotions trigger false hunger, unwarranted fears, or destructive habits.
            By eliminating these emotions and misconceptions, we restore control to our clients.
            Through hypnnosis, we neutralize driving forces, allowing authentic choices to emerge. The Duration of Change Hypnosis offers rapid solutions, yet misconceptions persist regarding its duration.
            While some experience profound changes in one session, others require 4-6 sessions.
            The duration hinges on the depth of beliefs and emotions fueling the problem.
            Each layer peeled away offers relief, guiding clients toward lasting transformation. The Sensation of Change What does change truly feel like? After the emotional clutter dissipates, change feels natural, like rediscovering one's essence.
            It's about returning control to the client, allowing them to make choices aligned with their authentic selves.
            Change, ultimately, feels liberating and timeless, fading problems into distant memories. In embracing hypnnosis, we embrace the essence of change — a journey back to the self, where control, choice, and freedom reign supreme.
            Explore this transformative path; your authentic self awaits. content: Search: 10 Ways Hypnosis Can Help You Lose Weight by Adam Fistler, BCH Maybe you heard that hypnosis can help you lose weight easily but you never quite understood how. You only heard vague notions that hypnosis could help you lose weight but never really knew what hypnosis could do for you. Below is a list of ten things hypnosis can do to help you easily get rid of weight and keep it off. 10. Eliminate Amnesic Eating (Mindless Eating) I've help a lot of clients lose weight, and one factor that is over looked is what I like to call amnesic eating. Amnesic eating is the little snacks grabbed here and there that people just simply forget they ate during the day. In fact if you were to go back over the course of the last couple of weeks I'm sure you could find things that you've had to eat which you totally forgot about. In most of the times when people eat these things, they really don't matter to that person. That person wouldn't have cared one way or the other if they would have eaten it or not. Worrying now about eating those things won't help you, but if you could have gone back and not eaten them, this could make a difference. Hypnosis can help you eliminate this amnesic eating. 9. Remove Guilt for Not Cleaning Your Plate Lots of times people get the message early on that they should clean their plate because there are starving people in the world. I'm sure when your parents told you that their message was not to waste food, not eat a lot and become overweight. Using hypnotic techniques we can help you with both being OK with pushing away after you are satisfied and with controlling the amount of food you take in the first place. 8. Remove Hunger Triggers Whether you are aware of it or not, there are also triggers than can make you feel hunger. Back a long time ago a doctor by the name of Ivan Pavlov discovered that every time he rang a bell, his dogs would begin to salivate. He found that ringing the bell in close proximity to delving food caused the dogs to associate the bell with eating. People can do much the same thing. Doing things such as eating in front of the TV can cause you to feel hungry every time you sit in front of the TV. Or perhaps just by driving by certain stores can cause you to feel hungry. We can help you identify these triggers and use hypnotic suggestion to remove them. 7. Reduce Over Eating and Binging Most of the time, over eating and binging are a method of distracting from an emotion. These are what sometimes are called coping behaviors. Instead of facing the emotion sometimes people binge to prevent them self from experiencing an emotion. We know that there is no amount of food that can ever satisfy an emotion. However we can help you neutralize the feelings that are causing the behaviors thus eliminating the behaviors. 6. End Internal Conflict We would all like to use will power to help us lose weight. However will power is exactly the wrong tool to use. Will power only stays with us as long as we want what we committed to more than we want to not exercise or to not stick to a diet. As you will learn you are tempted to overeat or eat the wrong things out of response to a feeling, even if you are not aware of that feeling. The desire to distract from that feeling becomes stronger than your desire to stick to your weight loss goals. Thus you continue to cycle of yo-yo dieting, or starting an exercise program then just quitting. Hypnosis can end this conflict so you can maintain healthy eating habits, and exercise. Wouldn't it be nice if your mind supported your efforts instead of undermining them? 5. Eliminate False Hunger Most of the food consumed by people wishing to lose weight is consumed when they are not physically hungry. Over time people begin to associate the physical sensations of emotions (which we call feelings) to being hungry. For example some people might get a feeling in their gut which they confuse with real hunger. These feelings and this behavior becomes almost automatic because the subconscious mind associate these feelings with hunger to protect us from remember or recalling unpleasant emotions. By using advanced hypnotic techniques we can eliminate false hunger, this reducing the amount of food consumed, all without conscious effort. 4. Reduce Physical Hunger We can reduce true physical hunger by helping our clients reduce stress. Stress contributes to physical hunger. In the physiology of the body, when stress levels goes up our liver releases more sugar into our body. This release of sugar is used to drive the fight or flight mechanism, to give us the energy to deal with a truly dangerous situation. But in our society if you are cut off in traffic or overworked, there is no way for this sugar to be burned off naturally. So when that sugar isn't used your body then releases insulin. Insulin is the hormone the body releases to store that sugar back into the body's cells. That unused sugar is then stored in our body cells, causing us to gain weight. Another byproduct of that insulin release is that an increase of insulin in our body causes physical hunger. If we were in an actual fight or flight situation, we would need to replace that used energy. But being stressed now that insulin release makes us physically hungry causes us to eat more. This cycle put together with unchecked stress can cause us to eat more than we really need to. Hypnotherapy allows our clients to better handle stress by helping eliminate the emotional cause of stress, and teaching our clients better relaxation techniques. 3. Effortless Exercise Hypnosis can help increase one desire to exercise. Using hypnosis we can help eliminate any blocks or barriers one has to exercising. If you to look at how a lot of people view exercise, you wouldn't want to do it either. Some people view exercise as tortuous, time consuming, painful, humiliating. However you view exercise we can just simply help you make it something that you just do. In fact I once had a client who used to view exercise as a competition. He had to go father, harder, and see the amount of calories burned exceed the amount he did yesterday or else he would be a failure. Every time he didn't top what he did the day before he would feel like a failure, and thus quit exercising regularly until he worked up his will power to do it again, usually months later. We transformed his view of exercise and now it's just something he simply does, and enjoys. 2. Easily Maintain Healthy Eating Habits Using hypnosis we can help you eliminate false hunger, and even reduce real physical hunger. By doing this it because easy to only eat when you are really physically hunger and to make good healthy choices. In fact you can still continue to eat the foods you love, because by neutralizing those feelings that caused you to over eat in the past, you will no longer have the desire to over eat thus you will reduce the amount of calories you intake naturally. 1. Improve the Way You Feel A lot of time times people figure that will begin to feel better about themselves after they lose weight. In most cases we find that the opposite is true. We find that improving a person mood and how the feel about themselves helps them lose weight. Consider those people who undergo plastic surgery to correct a perceived flaw, and after that flaw is corrected, they still aren't happy. People begin to fall into this trap that if only X happens than I will be happy. Then when X happens, then they need Y to happen in order to feel happy. In number of cases weight loss isn't about what you eat, but its about what's eating you. It is these emotions and the way a person feels about themselves which leads to over eating, not exercising and all things that contribute to keep the weight. By helping our clients feel better, maintain healthy eating habits and exercising regularly just naturally falls into place. content: Search: 10 Things to Consider When Choosing a Hypnotist by Adam Fistler, BCH When someone is looking into hypnosis as a means to overcome an issue, often times they become confused and overwhelmed by the number of hypnotist out there and the varying quality and skill levels of those practitioners. In this article I hope to clear up some confusion by listing ten things that you should consider when choosing a hypnotist, and give those looking into hypnosis services a better understanding of what to look for when choosing a hypnosis service provider. 10. The Hypnotist's Office When choosing a hypnotist you should consider the location and condition of the office the hypnotist is practicing from. Locations vary between practitioners. Commonly you may find hypnotist in office space, retail space, practicing out of their own house, to practicing out of places you would never dream of entering on your worst day. When choosing a hypnotist consider if you can really feel safe in his or her office. If you are not able to feel safe and comfortable this will greatly inhibit the depth of hypnosis you achieve and hurt your results. If a hypnotist is practicing in their own home, be sure that he or she can offer a distraction free environment. Find out if the practitioner has any pets and how they will keep the noise from these pets to a minimum. Consider also how they will limit distractions for ringing phones and television or others in the house. Be sure to consider your safety before entering a strange home and if you don't feel safe, leave. The origizination and cleanliness of the practitioner's office can also have subtle effects on how you perceive that practitioner. If a hypnotist office is dirty or unorganized it could cause you to question his or her professionalism and hurt the results that you receive. In the same vein, consider the professionalism of the practitioner. Is his or her office what you expected it to be? Is it a professional environment or is this person far out there? 9. Will Your Hypnotist Provide You with a Code of Ethics and Bill of Rights? One sign of a quality and reputable hypnosis practitioner is a person who will provide you with a code of ethics and a bill of rights. In some state it is mandatory for a practitioner to provide you with a code of ethics and Bill of Rights. The code of ethics will outline that practitioner's privacy policy, if he will share your records or discuss your case and outline his or her therapeutic approach. Professional hypnotist will adhere to a confidently policy and will not share your case with others. Another important aspect of a practitioner's code of ethics will outline any training and or degrees that he or she may hold. A quality hypnosis practitioner will also provide you will a Client Bill of Rights outline your rights as a client. At minimum this should include a right to see your records, a right to refuse service at anytime, a manner of redress for a dispute. If your practitioner belongs to a reputable hypnosis organization such as the National Guild of Hypnotist he or she will give you an option to seek redress through that group. Be sure to ask your practitioner for a copy of his or her code of ethics and Client Bill of Rights. If he or she does not have one you may want to reconsider using their services. 8. Does Your Hypnotist Fully and Honestly Disclose His or Her Training and Education? Included in either the practitioner's Code of Ethics or Client's Bill of Rights should be a full disclosure of your practitioner's education. Hypnosis and Hypnotherapy is it's own unique profession and requires it's own course of study and on going education that is different from that which is required from a doctor of psychologist. In fact you should know that most hypnotists are not psychologists and more psychologists are not hypnotists. Many in the public confuse the two services. The both have unique paths of learning and both take time, education and skill to master. That said there are psychologists and doctors who have taken the time to learn about hypnosis and apply it to their practices, however in these cases these practitioners only use hypnosis on a part time or occasional basis. When choosing a skilled hypnotist you should consider if your practitioner uses hypnosis on a full time basis, or on case to case basis. Currently in the United States there is no accredited degree for the practice of hypnosis. If you practitioner lists a degree in hypnosis, be sure to question where he or she has obtained it. There are hypnosis schools that give a degree in hypnosis called a Doctorate in Hypnosis or DCH, however these are not academically recognized in the United States. Be sure if a practitioner lists a degree in physiology or mental health to ask where he or she obtained that degree. There are practitioners who will obtain degrees from unaccredited schools mostly dealing with Mental Health of a PHD or PSY.D in psychology to gain more of a perceived credibility with the public. If a practitioner is reputable he or she will list whether or not a degree is from an alternate school. Hypnosis requires both good training, skill, practice and on going education in the latest and advanced techniques. When looking for a skilled hypnotist, look for one who has advanced training from a recognized hypnosis organization such as the National Guild of Hypnotists. Be sure to ask about any additional training the practitioner has and how he or she improves and keeps up to date on his practice. Hypnosis practitioners have a wide degree of skills and training. Be sure to choose one with good training and experience. There is a big difference between a hypnotist that goes to a weekend course on hypnosis to a hypnosis practitioner that spends the hundred hours to become certified and spends thousands more learning, taking training, reading and practicing hypnosis and achieving results with real live clients. Remember just about anyone can call themselves a hypnotist, but very few are considered professional. Just as there is a great disparity in the level of training a hypnotist might receive, there is also a great variance in the level of skill and technique used by a hypnotist. It is relatively easy to guide someone into the hypnotic state. In fact in just a few hours, you could train anyone to help guide others in hypnosis. It's that simple. Hypnosis is just a naturally occuring state that you go into everyday while watching TV or reading a book. It's what you do with the state that makes the difference from just experience hypnosis to achieving incredible results. Some hypnotists just deal with direct suggestion only. While direct suggestion is an important foundation to a good hypnotic process, it cannot be the only tool used. Direct suggestion hypnotists usually do their work in one or two sessions using pre written scripts dealing with your issue. Sometimes these scripts may not have anything to do with your issue at all. Due to poor or lack of training it is all these hypnotists know how to do. While this may work for some people, the results usually are temporary and give the impression that hypnosis is temporary and wares off. Other hypnosis practitioners will use such easy techniques as Emotional Freedom Techniques or simple Neurolinguistic Programming Techniques to try to affect change. While these techniques may be easy to do, these techniques usually only bring temporary relief to the problem and does not address the core reason for the issue. Sometimes you might even see hypnosis practices who take out full page ads in the news paper with a story about how someone quit smoking or lost weight. Most of these chain hypnosis practices hire some average Joe off of the street and give them minimal hypnosis training. They are then trained to their clients on a pair of headsets, a pair of lighted glasses, play a prerecorded CD, from people who don't even work at their hypnosis clinic, and leave the room. In these type of practices there is little to no contact with your hypnotist and everything is a cookie cutter process used for every client. For the thousand dollar packages these places lock you into, you could just buy a CD player and a few hypnosis CDs off of the internet a receive the same effect. The approach only provides temporary results for those who use this process, to those who need .the hypnotic booster. to maintain, to even no results because the core issues are never dealt with. The difference between hypnotist with simple training to one that truly studies hypnosis and the aspect of change can be like the difference between riding a tricycle and driving a Mercedes. Mastering a tricycle is much easier than mastering driving a car. A good skilled hypnotist has received advanced training and continues his study in the field of hypnosis. Good hypnosis starts by customizing the hypnosis process to the client, and using those advanced techniques to eliminate to real cause of the problem, not just treating symptoms. Sure it takes time, practice and skill to master those advanced techniques but by choosing a practitioner who has, you will increase you chances of obtaining permanent results. 7. Will Your Hypnotist Answer Your Questions? A good hypnosis practitioner will be patient and be happy to answer any questions that you may have, both in person and on the phone. Hypnosis is misunderstood by a lot of people so a good hypnotist or his staff should be happy to answer questions. Some places, when you phone them, the only way the will take to you is for you to come into a free consultation and sign up for a thousand dollar plus package. Choose a hypnotist you feel comfortable with and will be there for you if you have questions or concerns through out the process. 6. Does You Hypnotist Answer the Phone? If you were to take a moment and flip through the Yellow Pages and take the time to call every hypnotist listed, you would be surprised to learn how few of them will actually answer the phone. It's true. A mark of a professional hypnosis practice is one who will answer the phone, and answer your questions. If you do happen to get voice mail, gauge the time it takes to receive a call back. Is it more than one business day? If your hypnotist isn't there for you on the phone, how much will she be concerned about your success throughout the process? 5. Does Your Hypnotist Understand Your Issue? Does you hypnotist understand your issue and know how to get results? In some cases a medical referral is needed to work on certain issues such as pain management, diabetes and cancer. Does your practitoner know when your hypnosis treatment might interfere with a medical issue? A professional hypnotist knows how to contact your doctor and get a referral to work with your doctor on your issue. 4. Does Your Hypnotist Belong to an Established Hypnosis Origination? Does your hypnotist belong to an established hypnosis organization such as the National Guild of Hypnotist (NGH)? Established originations such as the NGH required minimum education standards for their hypnotist as well as continuing education. As well as establishing education guidelines, they also maintain ethical guideless as well as resolve disputes between clients and hypnotist. Belonging to an established origination help insures that your hypnotist maintains a high ethical standard as well as being highly trained. 3. Does Your Hypnotist Offer Convent Methods of Payment? A serious professional hypnotist is one who also offers several ways to pay for their clients. In this insightful article by Adam Fistler, a seasoned hypnotherapist, readers are provided with a comprehensive guide to navigate this selection process. It emphasizes the importance of framing intentions positively and visualizing the desired partner's qualities.
